title: Beyond Octopart: Why Part Search Isn't Enough Once You're Buying at Production Volume
summary: Octopart helps engineers decide which electronic components to use. Cofactr helps manufacturers execute the procurement required to keep building their products.
body_markdown:
## Part Search and Production Procurement Are Different Problems


You've successfully sourced the components for your first few prototype builds using Octopart. You found parts that met your design requirements, checked distributor availability, compared prices, and placed your orders. So far, so good.


Now your product is entering regular production, and the purchasing process is getting considerably more complicated. You have existing inventory to account for, open purchase orders to track, supplier pricing agreements to manage, and a contract manufacturer (CM) that expects complete kits to arrive on schedule. You may still be working with the same bill of materials (BOM), but your purchasing process has changed.


Octopart remains an excellent tool for component selection and sourcing intelligence. Cofactr addresses the ongoing procurement and material management responsibilities that come with manufacturing products repeatedly.


In this article, we'll explain what Octopart already does well and how production purchasing differs from sourcing a prototype BOM. We'll then look at where Cofactr fits into that process, including the areas where the platforms overlap.


By the end, you'll have a practical understanding of when Octopart meets your needs, when adding Cofactr makes sense, and why using both may be the best approach for your hardware team.


## Octopart Supports Electronic Component Selection


There's a lot to like about Octopart. You can use parametric search to narrow down components by electrical and mechanical specifications, then check which distributors have stock, what they're charging, and whether the part is active or heading toward end-of-life. You can also investigate alternatives and available compliance information before an awkward component choice gets baked into your design.


Its free[BOM Tool](https://octopart.com/en/bom-tool) takes that intelligence beyond individual part numbers. Uploading a BOM and Octopart helps match components, compare supplier offers, calculate costs at your planned build quantity, and prioritize preferred distributors. When you're ready to buy, it can hand selected items off to distributor carts. That's preferable to opening 37 browser tabs and hoping you haven't ordered the wrong package variant.


Octopart's[inventory-history](https://octopart.com/pulse/p/octopart-introduces-inventory-history-for-part-trends) views also let you inspect three or twelve months of distributor stock trends. A component with 10,000 units available today may deserve a closer look if inventory has been falling steadily for months.


Octopart is part of Altium's design ecosystem, which makes sense. Component selection belongs in engineering decisions, preferably before someone finishes routing a board around a part that's impossible to source.

## What Changes When You Move Into Repeatable Production?


Suppose you've got a 200-line BOM and need parts for 25 prototype boards. Octopart helps you assess sourceability and buy what you need for the build. You might have some leftover stock, easily managed with a spreadsheet and a few labeled boxes.


Now production wants another 500 boards next month, followed by 800 the month after. Your enterprise resource planning (ERP) or material requirements planning (MRP) system may generate purchase recommendations based on the build schedule, inventory already on hand, and orders suppliers haven't delivered yet. You need to act on individual material requirements as they come due, rather than simply buying the entire BOM again every time.


Say your next build requires 1,600 connectors, with 700 already on a confirmed PO and 300 in the stockroom. Assuming the incoming order arrives on time, you need to buy 600 more. Ordering 1,600 would leave you with quite a collection of connectors.


Supplier restrictions complicate things further. The[best published price](https://www.cofactr.com/articles/beyond-the-quote-how-cofactr-calculates-true-landed-cost) may come with a 5,000-piece minimum order, a full-reel requirement, or a delivery date that misses your build. Add negotiated pricing, freight, tariffs, supplier approvals, and packaging requirements, and simple price comparisons become less useful.


After purchasing, somebody has to chase acknowledgments, track shortages, reconcile receipts, and get the right quantities to manufacture. No magic volume threshold triggers this transition. It happens when the coordination work becomes a serious use of your team's time.


## Cofactr Supports Procurement Execution


Cofactr is designed to take a material requirement through purchasing and, when you use our 3PL services, all the way to a build-ready kit. That's the work that tends to land on the desk of whichever engineer was unfortunate enough to be good at spreadsheets.


### **Executing Purchases Across Suppliers**


Cofactr evaluates supplier offers in the context of actual buying constraints, including approved sources, negotiated pricing, minimum order quantities (MOQs), order multiples, shipping, tariffs, and packaging. It can coordinate orders across suppliers, saving you the pleasure of repeating the checkout routine at every distributor.


A low unit price loses some of its charm when you need 800 ICs and the supplier insists on selling you 5,000. Cofactr's landed-cost calculations account for the cost of purchasing under those terms and compare options against the delivery schedule. You get a clearer picture of what the order will cost, including expenses that don't appear in a distributor's headline price.


### **Managing Orders and Deliveries**


Cofactr supports PO management, order tracking, and supplier coordination. That matters when fifteen shipments are due and your CM has already scheduled assembly.


For teams using ERP or product lifecycle management (PLM) systems, Cofactr also offers integrations that connect BOM, purchasing, and inventory information with existing workflows. Depending on the[configuration](https://support.cofactr.com/articles/4081898446-cofactr-platform-api-documentation) , that can cut down the spreadsheet re-entry between engineering plans and purchasing orders.


### **Managing Material After Purchase**


A tracking number showing *delivered* doesn't mean your components are ready to go through assembly. They still need to be received, identified, inspected as required, and stored properly. Improperly stored moisture-sensitive parts can suffer damage during reflow, a terrible time to find out your storage process needs work.


Cofactr's managed inventory services cover receiving, component authentication, inventory storage, lot traceability, kitting, and delivery to a CM or production facility. Where the program requires it, associated records can include packing slips, certificates of conformance, lot and date codes, and kit verification.

## Where Octopart and Cofactr Overlap and Why They Aren't Substitutes


Both platforms work with component prices and availability, so there will naturally be some overlap. Octopart helps you examine what's available in the market and compare published offers. Cofactr incorporates supplier information into purchase decisions that account for your actual requirements and buying rules.


Supplier selection works similarly. Octopart helps engineers find distributors and prioritize preferred vendors. Cofactr handles the operational constraints around which suppliers you're permitted to buy from and how orders should be executed.


BOMs are another shared starting point. Octopart's BOM Tool is excellent for sourceability and costing analysis. Cofactr can use BOM information as part of an ongoing procurement and inventory workflow.


Altium deserves credit for covering that middle ground between CAD and NPI. The distinction with Cofactr becomes clearest after the prototypes, when repeat orders need managing and material needs receiving, tracking, storing, and delivering. Those activities are central to Cofactr's service model.


## When Should You Use Octopart, Cofactr, or Both?


### **Use Octopart when you're choosing parts or evaluating a BOM**


It's a strong fit when you're comparing specifications, checking lifecycle status, researching alternates, looking at distributor stock, or buying material for a prototype. Keep using it to monitor component availability during production, too.


### **Use Cofactr when the procurement execution starts eating your calendar**


Recurring buy requirements, approved-supplier rules, negotiated rates, multiple open POs, and material traceability are all signs that you need procurement execution capabilities. The same applies when your CM expects organized kits and your team is currently trying to manage that with spreadsheets and optimism.


### **Use both when engineering and operations need different tools**


Engineering can use Octopart to make sensible component decisions while Cofactr handles purchasing and material operations.[Altium and Cofactr](https://resources.altium.com/p/cofactr-partners-altium) have even partnered to connect Altium 365 BOM information with Cofactr's supply-chain workflows.


## Beyond Part Search, Into Procurement Execution


Octopart continues to earn its keep throughout a product's life, especially when you're checking availability or weighing an alternate. As production becomes repeatable, procurement also involves supplier commitments, inventory accounting, order follow-through, and the physical handling that gets components onto the assembly line.


Octopart helps engineers decide which electronic components to use. Cofactr helps manufacturers execute the procurement required to keep building their products. When you know which problem you're trying to solve, it's much easier to spend your time and budget on the right tool.

## Frequently Asked Questions


**What is the difference between Octopart and Cofactr?**


Octopart specializes in electronic component search, pricing comparisons, and BOM analysis. Cofactr manages production procurement, supplier orders, inventory storage, component traceability, kitting, and material deliveries.


**How does Octopart help with electronic component sourcing?**


Octopart provides parametric component search, distributor pricing, stock availability, lifecycle information, and alternatives. Its free BOM Tool also supports component matching, cost calculations, and purchasing preparation.


**When should manufacturers switch from Octopart to Cofactr?**


Manufacturers should consider Cofactr when recurring production requires coordinated purchasing, multiple supplier orders, negotiated pricing, inventory management, or scheduled material deliveries to contract manufacturers.


**Can I use Octopart and Cofactr together?**


Yes. Engineering teams can use Octopart for component selection and availability research, while Cofactr handles procurement execution, inventory tracking, supplier coordination, and production material management.


**How does Cofactr calculate electronic component purchasing costs?**


Cofactr evaluates supplier offers using negotiated pricing, minimum order quantities, order multiples, freight, tariffs, and packaging requirements to calculate landed costs against production delivery schedules.


**What is the best tool for managing electronic component BOMs?**


Octopart works well for BOM sourceability analysis, component comparisons, and prototype costing. Cofactr supports ongoing BOM-driven purchasing requirements, supplier coordination, and inventory management during production.


**Why does electronic component procurement become more complicated during production?**


Recurring builds require manufacturers to account for existing inventory, outstanding purchase orders, supplier lead times, minimum order quantities, and scheduled deliveries while avoiding unnecessary component purchases.


**Does Cofactr offer electronic component inventory management and kitting?**


Yes. Cofactr provides managed receiving, component authentication, inventory storage, lot traceability, kitting, and delivery services, helping manufacturers prepare materials for scheduled assembly at contract manufacturing facilities.
